scenarios.name: coil_modulating_on_setpoint
scenarios.description: Ordinary mechanical cooling: SAT is on its 13 °C setpoint with the valve at 65%. The loop has reserve in both directions, which is what a healthy cooling coil looks like

scenarios.name: valve_wide_open_holding_setpoint
scenarios.description: The valve is at 100% and SAT is 0.5 °C high — a coil sized close to its design point on a design day. Half a degree is inside eSAT, so this is a unit at capacity, not a unit that has lost capacity

scenarios.name: sat_error_exactly_at_threshold
scenarios.description: Threshold edge: SAT − SATSP = 1.0 °C exactly, the whole eSAT allowance, with the valve at 100%. `spMiss` is a strict `>`, so an error sitting precisely on the sensor allowance reads healthy

scenarios.name: sat_error_just_over_threshold
scenarios.description: Threshold edge, other side: 1.1 °C above setpoint at 100% valve clears the strict comparison, and the alarm asserts one alarm_delay (1800 s) later

scenarios.name: valve_exactly_at_full_threshold
scenarios.description: Threshold edge: a 5 °C setpoint miss with the valve parked on exactly 99.0%. `clgFull` is a strict `>`, so a command sitting on cc_full_threshold does not count as saturated and the rule stays silent

scenarios.name: valve_just_over_full_threshold
scenarios.description: Threshold edge, other side: the same 5 °C miss with the valve at 99.5% clears the strict comparison and alarms after alarm_delay

scenarios.name: coil_saturated_and_missing_setpoint
scenarios.description: The valve is wide open and SAT is stuck 5 °C above setpoint — the control loop has asked for everything and the temperature has not moved. Chilled water too warm, a fouled or undersized coil, or a valve that reports open and is not: capacity, supply, or sensor, never tuning

scenarios.name: morning_pulldown_clears_before_delay
scenarios.description: Transient: the valve pins at 100% and SAT runs 5 °C high while the coil pulls the building down after a warm night, reaching setpoint at t = 1200. A pulldown is shorter than alarm_delay, so nothing alarms

scenarios.name: fault_clears_when_chilled_water_returns
scenarios.description: A saturated valve missing setpoint alarms at 1800 s; the chiller comes back at t = 3000 and SAT reaches setpoint. `TrueDelay` has no off-delay, so the alarm drops on that tick

scenarios.name: valve_backs_off_before_delay
scenarios.description: Transient: SAT stays 5 °C high but the valve modulates back to 85% at t = 1200. A loop with reserve left is a loop still working, so persistence restarts and no alarm follows — the saturation half is what makes the setpoint miss evidence of a defect
